events.continuity_hook: The graduation trip remains intact, but the later arrival requires a fresh check of airport-to-hotel timing and an after-hours arrival arrangement.
events.interaction_goal: Verify that the adjusted flight still leaves a workable Friday arrival, notify the hotel of the late check-in, and confirm that no part of the reservation needs to be rebooked.
events.scenario_brief: The late-Friday itinerary for Avery and her wife is booked, but the airline has moved their arrival 55 minutes later and the hotel desk closes overnight unless notified. The new timing still permits Saturday dinner if the flight operates as scheduled, while the Monday return and three-night room remain confirmed.

events.continuity_hook: The pickup appointment is fixed, but the outbound day and whether Avery can return Wednesday night remain unresolved.
events.interaction_goal: Compare Tuesday and early-Wednesday outbound flights together with late-Wednesday and Thursday return options, identifying combinations that allow enough time for the museum appointment and crate departure.
events.scenario_brief: Avery is assigned to oversee a collection pickup at a Dallas museum on Wednesday at 10:00 a.m. and must remain until the sealed crates leave late that afternoon. She will travel alone from Atlanta; a same-day outbound would require a very early departure, while arriving Tuesday would add a hotel night, and the carrier cannot yet guarantee that loading will finish in time for the last Wednesday flight.

events.continuity_hook: The Tuesday flight is now favored and a one-night stay is required; the return depends on final freight timing.
events.interaction_goal: Choose an available Tuesday-night hotel using full cost and travel time to the museum, and compare the Wednesday-night flight with the Thursday fallback before booking the itinerary.
events.scenario_brief: The freight company now expects the crates to leave by 5:00 p.m. Wednesday, making the final nonstop to Atlanta feasible if loading stays on schedule. Avery selects a Tuesday evening outbound for a less compressed arrival and needs one hotel night with a practical route to the museum, while keeping a Thursday morning return as a fallback until the carrier confirms the loading window.

events.continuity_hook: The Tuesday outbound and one-night hotel remain confirmed; only the return must be finalized now that loading will end earlier.
events.interaction_goal: Replace the Thursday fallback with the workable Wednesday evening flight, verify the final fare and arrival time, and ensure the itinerary reflects the correct return date.
events.scenario_brief: Two days before departure, the freight carrier confirms a 4:30 p.m. release, so Avery can use the Wednesday evening return. The fare previously reviewed is still available, but the booking record currently retains the Thursday flight that was held as the fallback.

events.continuity_hook: The trip length and destination are established, while the exact weekend, flight pairing, local transportation, and lodging area remain open.
events.interaction_goal: Compare complete trip totals for both date windows, including flights for two, local transportation, and representative oceanfront and inland lodging, then select the stronger window for detailed hotel research.
events.scenario_brief: Avery and her wife plan a four-night anniversary trip to Carlsbad in early summer and will share one room. They can travel during either of two adjacent Thursday-to-Monday windows, need flights from Atlanta and local transportation, and have not decided whether staying directly by the ocean is worth a higher total than lodging several blocks inland.

events.continuity_hook: Flights and dates are fixed, leaving the shared hotel as the main unresolved part of the anniversary trip.
events.interaction_goal: Verify beach access, balcony and view details, complete four-night totals, parking costs, availability, and cancellation terms, then narrow the options to a bookable room.
events.scenario_brief: Avery and her wife choose the later Thursday-to-Monday window and reserve their flights. They now need to compare available four-night rooms, including one oceanfront property and two within walking distance of the beach; room descriptions differ on whether a balcony has an ocean view, and nightly rates do not include all taxes and parking charges.
